messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: High 5xx + timeouts observed for /v1/runtime requests in us-west-2. p95 and p99 jumped at 12:34 UTC after recent deploy. paging: Maya (SRE)
Maya (SRE): I see the spike. p99 latency ~3.2s -> 18s, error rate ~3.1% 5xx (gateway+upstream timeouts). Started right after canary cutover at 12:30.
Ben (eng-runtime): rolling deploy #2026-03-15-1 went to 100% at 12:29:43. logs show lots of connection timeouts to the model host pool.
Claire (oncall): Are customers impacted? any high-traffic corp tenant calls?
metrics-bot: Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/abc123/runtime-latency - p99 spike highlighted. Request volume steady. Error budget burn rate high.
Tasha (support): getting inbound tickets from two enterprise customers complaining about timeouts in their production services. Escalated to SEs.
Sam (prod-sre): quick check of kvcache stats shows massive eviction and refill traffic on the runtime nodes around 12:31->12:35. likely cold-warm transition after the deploy changed model variant/kv-layout.
Maya (SRE): that matches traces: many requests hit model cold-starts and then ttl/warmup loops, causing long tail and upstream timeouts.
Ben (eng-runtime): hypothesis: new compile path introduced a larger KV footprint and sequence-length routing changed, evicting hot prefixes. fallback route to smaller-quantized variant wasn't wired in the canary.
Claire (oncall): mitigation options: 1) rollback to previous release, 2) route traffic to dedicated fallback pool, 3) throttle/buffer at gateway to protect model pool. Which is fastest?
Ben (eng-runtime): fastest is rollback. I can trigger immediate revert to release 2026-03-15-0. Initiating in 2m unless someone objects.
Maya (SRE): start rollback and also enable prefix caching on edge to reduce repeated cold misses.
Sam (prod-sre): I'll open a temporary route to the older model-variant for high-SLA customers in the meantime.
Claire (oncall): ok do it. Claire (oncall) pinned: Initiating rollback now.
ops-bot: Command received: `deploy revert --release=2026-03-15-0 --env=prod --strategy=immediate` by Ben (eng-runtime) at 12:38:21 UTC.
Ben (eng-runtime): running smoke checks on a small slice to confirm.
Maya (SRE): meanwhile enabling edge prefix cache TTL extension: `edgectl set-prefix-ttl --service=runtime --ttl=30m` to reduce load.
metrics-bot: After TTL extension, cache hit rate improved 12:40 -> 12:43 (cache-hit +14%). p95 dropped to 2.1s.
ops-bot: Rollback progress: 25% -> 50% -> 75% -> 100% completed at 12:44:03 UTC.
Sam (prod-sre): routing fallback for top-enterprise tenants active at 12:41:10.
Maya (SRE): logs show inflight requests dropping and fewer upstream timeouts. sample: ```
[12:42:58] runtime-12 WARN upstream_timeout id=abcd1234 host=model-host-23 elapsed=16.8s
[12:43:05] runtime-09 INFO cache_hit id=efgh5678 prefix=customer-ords status=200
```
Tasha (support): notified customer SEs that we rolled back and are monitoring. Customers report reduced errors.
metrics-bot: p99 returned to baseline ~0.9s by 12:46. Error rate back under 0.2%.
Claire (oncall): thanks team. Postmortem owners? Ben and Maya to investigate root cause and a fix (kv layout + canary safeguards). Sam to validate routing fallback automation.
Ben (eng-runtime): I'll add a preflight check to verify KV footprint and warmup plan before rollout. Also will block canary promotion if evictions spike > X.
Maya (SRE): I'll run replays against the canary variant with cold-warm traffic pattern and produce an eval report.
Claire (oncall): handing off to Sam for post-incident monitoring and compliance notes. Sam (prod-sre) takes over. :thumbsup:
Sam (prod-sre): taking it. I'll keep the channel updated for 2h monitoring window.
incident-bot: Incident acknowledged and marked "mitigated" at 12:47:10 UTC. Pager cleared.
Tasha (support): customer tickets updated. flagging for follow-up comms with affected enterprise accounts. :eyes: 
Ben (eng-runtime): quick action items: `#1 add canary eviction threshold`, `#2 kv warmup step in deploy pipeline`, `#3 route fallback test` - will create GH issues.
Maya (SRE): tagging for evals and telemetry: will attach traces and sample ids to the postmortem.
Claire (oncall): handoff complete at 12:48 UTC. Good job. :tada:
